# QEVA roadmap

The roadmap is ordered by epistemic and operational dependency. Page count,
traffic, model output, and corpus size are not progress if QEVA cannot explain
what a record means, where it came from, what checked it, and how to recover it.

## 0.5 — shipped in this archive

- One offline Explore → Lab → inspect → fork/export loop.
- Six declarative mechanisms: modular projection, logistic sensitivity,
  coarse-grained signal, local/global search, Collatz orbit, finite maps.
- Run, mathematical Diff, Observer Switch, bounded Sweep, and bounded Attack.
- Exact run, engine-artifact, analyzer-artifact, subject, and proof bindings.
- Strict parameter/kernel/analyzer/resource contracts and negative fixtures.
- Append-only corrective revisions; no rewrite of 148 inherited v0.4 records.
- Harvester 0.2 with bounded responses, atomic writes, rights gates, raw fixity,
  retrieval events, preserved source assertions, and quarantine tests.
- One-current-per-ID and all-revision exports for objects, experiments, and
  analyzers; typed legacy relations remain visibly candidate.
- Data-only BagIt recovery subset, print core, deterministic outer package, and
  split canonical/runtime/preservation verification.

This does not mean QEVA contains all mathematics, has scraped the internet,
runs a production corpus, has independent mirrors, or is a durable institution.

## 0.6 — corpus pilot

- Add resumable snapshot readers for OpenAlex/Crossref and checkpointed arXiv
  metadata; use Common Crawl indexes only for bounded discovery.
- Resolve DOI, arXiv, ORCID, Wikidata, and repository identifiers without
  title-only merging.
- Run a licensed, reproducible 100,000-work pilot with storage/resource reports,
  rights decisions, failures, and independently replayed fixtures.
- Establish deletion/takedown, robots, retry, and provider-change procedures.

**Exit test:** a clean operator can reproduce the pilot and explain the source,
rights state, transformation, and fixity of every retained byte.

## 0.7 — mathematical extraction and review

- Preserve TeX/MathML structure only where rights permit.
- Segment definitions, assumptions, results, proof references,
  counterexamples, algorithms, and open questions.
- Bind every candidate to an exact source locator and extractor artifact.
- Build disagreement, duplicate, framework, and human-review queues.

**Exit test:** reviewers can accept, reject, split, correct, or defer every
candidate without relying on opaque model memory or auto-promotion.

## 0.8 — formal and executable bridges

- Import exact declaration and dependency identities from formal libraries at
  pinned commits.
- Treat informal↔formal correspondence as reviewed mappings, not equality.
- Archive kernels, compilers, environments, and replay instructions.
- Replace host-dependent transcendental examples with specified portable
  approximations in new kernel revisions.

**Exit test:** an independent implementation replays a useful formal subset and
matches published certificates from archived inputs.

## 0.9 — world history graph

- Add works, manuscripts, translations, traditions, people, institutions,
  regions, uncertain date intervals, and disputed priority claims.
- Recruit regionally diverse historians and publish dissent/correction paths.
- Mechanically prevent citation/history edges from becoming proof dependencies.

**Exit test:** historical paths are source-backed, uncertainty-preserving, and
reviewable in original scripts and languages where feasible.

## 1.0 — federated public institution

- Ratify a narrow constitution, contributor covenant, conflict process,
  transparent budgets, and succession/hostile-fork rules.
- Operate at least five independently administered mirrors across three legal
  jurisdictions and organizational families.
- Publish multi-party signed release witnesses and complete two cold-recovery
  drills with the primary operator removed.
- Deposit physical, print, and offline digital snapshots with named custodians.

**Exit test:** QEVA remains downloadable, verifiable, and governable after the
founder, domain, main server, and primary organization are absent.

## Century-scale loop

Every generation must migrate media and cryptography, preserve prior encodings,
translate the recovery core, test cold restoration, rotate custody, audit legal
rights, and publish failures. “Store once for a million years” is not a credible
milestone; practiced succession is the durable mechanism.
